summary: Validated draft (validate --run <run> --submission update.json → valid=true). One sourced authority-transition defect: the TimeoutNow handler (raft.go:2209-2214) unconditionally clears the known leader, sets the node to Candidate and sets candidateFromLeadershipTransfer, while TimeoutNowRequest (commands.go:204-208) carries no Term and checkRPCHeader (raft.go:43-67) only bounds protocol version — so there is no membership, term-freshness or sender-is-leader condition on the one RPC that can force a leadership transfer. Because that flag makes electSelf stamp LeadershipTransfer=true (raft.go:296,1993) and makes voters skip the known-leader rejection (raft.go:1650-1656), a TimeoutNow that no longer reflects live leadership (or one from a protocol-compatible non-member) induces a winnable election that deposes the incumbent leader. Sibling handlers requestVote/requestPreVote do reject non-members (raft.go:1639-1649, 1755-1761), so the guard is missing specifically here. Recorded as three Behaviors/Facts, an active investigation with discriminator/refutation, and an 'explained' interpretation with counterevidence and honest limitations (mechanism source-established; experiment capacity for this run was exhausted, so no execution witness was retained). I also checked and discarded two adjacent suspicions that turned out to be protected: installSnapshot's missing setLastLog is compensated by getLastEntry/getLastIndex using lastSnapshotIndex, and commitment.recalculate's median index is correct for even voter counts.
